items.script_text: A true zero-percent introductory APR is different.
items.severity: MATERIAL: changes a defined financial term into a date word in the key comparison beat
evidence: Unprompted whisper.cpp small.en transcript of the full file: 'A true 0% introductory April is different.' (token p=0.993).
Isolated re-decodes of 36.80-39.70 s: default beam, greedy (bs1/bo1), temperature 0.4 and tail-only 37.60-39.70 s all return 'April'.
Decoder prompt deliberately biased toward 'APR, annual percentage rate, A.P.R.' still returns 'April' on the isolated sentence.

Acoustic segmentation (LPC formants, 10 kHz): [ae-I] 38.63-38.74 s, /p/ closure 38.76-38.84 s, then [r-schwa-dark l] 38.85-39.02 s with lowered F3 ~1.6-1.7 kHz and F2 ~0.95-1.08 kHz, then 'is' at ~39.10 s.
No /i:/ ('pee') after the /p/ release: this voice's own /i:/ in '-ry' shows F2 ~2.0 kHz (38.56-38.62 s); no such segment occurs, nor an open 'ar' vowel (F1 >= ~650 Hz).
Post-release material lasts ~0.17 s, enough for '-ril' but not for two spelled letter names 'P' + 'R'.
items.limitations: No human listening pass was possible in this session; the finding rests on ASR agreement across five decodes plus acoustic-phonetic segmentation.
items.action: Owner to regenerate the MP3 with the TTS input written so the voice spells the letters (for example 'A-P-R' or 'A.P.R.', or SSML say-as characters), then re-run build/align_audio.py. The supplied MP3 was not edited.

other_terms_note: Recognized as the scripted words with ASR token probability 0.78-0.999; 'zero-percent' surfaces as '0%' (spoken 'zero percent').
